Cryptography

Root Certificate

A self-signed digital certificate that identifies a trusted Certificate Authority (CA) at the apex of a certification chain, serving as a trust anchor for all subordinate certificates.

Quick answer: A self-signed digital certificate that identifies a trusted Certificate Authority (CA) at the apex of a certification chain, serving as a trust anchor for all subordinate certificates.

Questions and answers

What is Root Certificate?

In this glossary, Root Certificate refers to: A self-signed digital certificate that identifies a trusted Certificate Authority (CA) at the apex of a certification chain, serving as a trust anchor for all subordinate certificates.

How is Root Certificate used in cybersecurity?

In cybersecurity communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Browsers and operating systems include root certificates in their trust stores to validate all subordinate CA and end-entity certificates."

Definition

A self-signed digital certificate that identifies a trusted Certificate Authority (CA) at the apex of a certification chain, serving as a trust anchor for all subordinate certificates.

Operational example

Browsers and operating systems include root certificates in their trust stores to validate all subordinate CA and end-entity certificates.
